headline: US September payrolls came in at 29,000 against about 90,000 expected, cutting October Fed hike odds to near 37 percent from roughly 70 percent and lifting the Nasdaq Composite 1.19 percent, while Indian markets stayed shut for Gandhi Jayanti and the 10 year Treasury yield held at 5.28 percent.

summary.us: September nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against estimates clustered near 90,000 and the unemployment rate rose to 4.2 percent, which cut October Fed hike pricing to about 37 percent from roughly 70 percent earlier in the week and pulled the 10 year Treasury yield back from an intraday 5.23 percent, its highest since June 2007. The S and P 500 added 0.73 percent to 7,722.72, the Nasdaq Composite 1.19 percent to 27,190.86 on a semiconductor revival and an intraday record in Nvidia, and the VIX fell 6.59 percent to 15.31, with Tesla up 4.65 percent on 486,532 third quarter deliveries.
summary.india: NSE and BSE were shut on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti, so the latest close is Thursday 1 October, when the Nifty 50 fell 0.88 percent to 22,421.95 for a fourth straight decline and the Sensex lost 571 points to 71,909.70, with Bank Nifty down 0.33 percent to 54,450.75 and Nifty Auto off about 3 percent. Foreign institutions sold 9,484 crore rupees against 10,042 crore rupees of domestic buying that day, after about 44,000 crore rupees of foreign selling in September, with October rate increase fears, 91 dollar crude and the rupee at 96.30 named as the drivers.
summary.global: Hong Kong reopened from its holiday to the largest fall since 23 March, the Hang Seng down 2.60 percent to 23,972.29 with HSBC off 5.7 percent and no Stock Connect support while mainland China stayed closed for Golden Week, and the Nikkei 225 fell 0.94 percent after Tokyo core CPI for September printed 2.7 percent against 2.4 percent expected, lifting December Bank of Japan increase pricing to about 82 percent. Europe closed higher, the DAX up 1.17 percent and the FTSE 100 up 0.32 percent, as energy prices eased on reports France proposed an IEA release of 50 million barrels each of diesel and crude, leaving WTI 1.73 percent lower at 91.26 dollars, gold 0.72 percent lower at 4,172.10 dollars and the dollar index at 101.92.

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms for four days and then handed them back on Friday. The US 10 year Treasury yield touched about 5.23 percent intraday midweek, described in coverage as the highest since June 2007, which pushed the dollar index to fresh 2026 highs, sent gold about 3.5 percent lower on the week and left the Dow down 1.3 percent and the S and P 500 down 0.3 percent even after Friday's bounce. Friday's September payrolls print of 29,000 against about 90,000 expected, with unemployment at 4.2 percent, cut October Fed hike pricing to near 37 percent from roughly 70 percent earlier in the week, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 percent with Nvidia at an intraday record and Tesla up 4.65 percent on 486,532 third quarter deliveries. India had the worse week and the shorter one: the Nifty fell 2.78 percent to 22,421.95 by Thursday's close, within 0.4 percent of its 52 week low, on rate increase fears, 91 dollar crude and foreign selling of about 44,000 crore rupees in September, before markets shut on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti. Hong Kong reopened from its own holiday to its largest fall since March with HSBC down 5.7 percent, Tokyo slipped as September core CPI came in at 2.7 percent against 2.4 percent expected, and silver lost 5.5 percent while copper held near records on tight supply. Next week turns on the 7 October FOMC minutes and the Reserve Bank decision the same day, with TCS opening India's earnings season on 8 October and the Strait of Hormuz still the swing factor for oil.

hgf.outlook_1y: Citi reaffirmed a three month target of 15,000 dollars a tonne. Goldman Sachs raised its 2027 average forecast to 13,800 dollars a tonne and separately sees a 10,000 to 11,000 dollar range for 2026 and 2027 in an October 2025 note. Macquarie sees a floor near 11,000 dollars by the third quarter of 2027 and Chile's Cochilco lifted its 2027 outlook to 5.10 dollars a pound.
hgf.outlook_lt: Goldman Sachs expects deficits outside the United States of 640,000 tonnes in 2026 and 170,000 tonnes in 2027 on tightening inventories, constrained mine supply and expanding strategic demand. clf.outlook_lt: Goldman Sachs sketches Brent above 120 dollars in 2027 if Gulf output stays 4 million barrels a day below pre war levels, which is not its base case. J.P. Morgan's bear case puts Brent at 42 dollars in 2027 absent voluntary supply restraint. WTI settled 1.73 percent lower at 91.26 dollars after reports that France proposed an IEA release of 50 million barrels each of diesel and crude, against tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz falling to single digits.
